abstract_sentences.text: The long-output context generation of large reasoning models enables extended chain of thought (CoT) but also drives rapid growth of the key–value (KV) cache, quickly overwhelming GPU memory.
abstract_sentences.transition: opens the scope and resource bottleneck

abstract_sentences.text: To address this challenge, we propose ThinKV, a thought-adaptive KV cache compression framework.
ThinKV is based on the observation that attention sparsity reveals distinct thought types with varying importance within the CoT.

evidence.anchor: attention sparsity reveals distinct thought types

abstract_sentences.transition: states the mechanism used by the named method

abstract_sentences.text: It applies a hybrid quantization–eviction strategy, assigning token precision by thought importance and progressively evicting tokens from less critical thoughts as reasoning trajectories evolve.
abstract_sentences.comparison: thought importance orders precision and eviction

abstract_sentences.text: Furthermore, to implement ThinKV, we design a kernel that extends PagedAttention to enable efficient reuse of evicted tokens’ memory slots, eliminating compaction overheads.
abstract_sentences.transition: adds the system realization after the algorithm

abstract_sentences.text: Extensive experiments on DeepSeek-R1-Distill, GPT-OSS, and NVIDIA AceReason across mathematics and coding benchmarks show that ThinKV achieves near-lossless accuracy with less than 5% of the original KV cache, while improving performance with up to 5.8× higher inference throughput over SoTA baselines.

evidence.anchor: less than 5% of the original KV cache

experimental_design.name: Research question and prelisted hypotheses

experimental_design.name: Models and benchmarks
experimental_design.description: Evaluates DeepSeek-R1-Distill, GPT-OSS, QwQ, AceReason-Nemotron, and MobileLLM-R1 on AIME, MATH-500, GSM8K, and LiveCodeBench.

experimental_design.name: Calibration data
experimental_design.description: Randomly samples 100 prompts from s1K for calibration.

experimental_design.name: Fixed hyperparameters
experimental_design.description: Uses |T|=3, |L*|=4, tau=128, group size 16, R={64,32,16,8,4}, and CT block size 8.

experimental_design.name: Baselines
experimental_design.description: Uses H2O, RaaS, R-KV, LazyEviction, KIVI, and PM-KVQ; system results also split R-KV sequential and overlapped gather.

experimental_design.name: Hardware and generation budget
experimental_design.description: Runs on one NVIDIA A100 80GB GPU and one NVIDIA GH200 Superchip, with maximum generation length 32K tokens.

experimental_design.description: For each question, generates 8 independent responses and computes pass@1 as the mean correctness indicator.

experimental_design.description: Throughput and latency are averages across 3 independent runs.

result_inventory.claim: ThinKV reaches competitive accuracy at substantially smaller KV memory shares than eviction baselines on the Figure 8 grid.
result_inventory.value: At 1024 tokens: <3.67% of FullKV memory; other methods require >12% for similar accuracy. On AIME, R1-Llama-8B and AceReason-14B have <4% drop at about 1.3% cache.
result_inventory.comparison: H2O, RaaS, R-KV, LazyEviction, and FullKV across AIME, LiveCodeBench, and MATH-500.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Pass@1 mean over 8 independent responses per question; no interval or test reported.
result_inventory.author_explanation: Hybrid, thought-adaptive compression preserves important reasoning information.
result_inventory.alternative_explanation: Model-, budget-, and task-specific curves are not a single fully matched setting.
result_inventory.treatment_of_alternative: Uses a common budget grid and multiple model/task panels but reports no uncertainty bands.

result_inventory.claim: ThinKV loses less accuracy than uniform/progressive quantization baselines at similar reported average precision.
result_inventory.value: R1-Qwen-14B AIME: FullKV 53.33, KIVI 40.00, PM-KVQ 43.33, ThinKV 50.00; LiveCodeBench: 47.90, 34.56, 41.97, 45.84.
result_inventory.comparison: KIVI and PM-KVQ on R1-Qwen-14B; Table 1 also contains QwQ-32B.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Accuracy point estimates; no interval or test reported.
result_inventory.author_explanation: TBQ gives precision according to thought-type importance.
result_inventory.alternative_explanation: Precision and eviction budget differ by method.
result_inventory.treatment_of_alternative: Table reports bit width and ThinKV k=1024, but does not fully normalize every method parameter.

claim_closure.claim: Attention sparsity supports a three-type thought decomposition.
claim_closure.method_response: Definition 1 and KDE thresholds operationalize phi; decode refresh uses selected layers.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figures 3 and 14 plus Figure 11(a) show the empirical structure and |T| ablation.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion restates decomposition into reasoning, execution, and transition segments.

claim_closure.claim: Thought importance should control KV precision.
claim_closure.origin: Introduction contribution: Think Before you Quantize
claim_closure.method_response: TBQ maps R/E/T importance to precision formats.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 4, Figure 11(b), Figure 16, and Table 10 connect importance/sensitivity to formats and accuracy.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion says thought-aware quantization sustains accuracy under high compression.

claim_closure.claim: Transition-thought dynamics justify progressive segment-level eviction.
claim_closure.origin: Introduction contribution: Think Before You Evict
claim_closure.method_response: TBE uses transition thought ct and an annealing retention schedule.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 5 presents associations; Figure 10(b) and Table 5 present eviction behavior and call rate.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion includes thought-aware eviction in the mechanism summary.

claim_closure.claim: CT avoids expensive compaction during non-contiguous eviction.
claim_closure.method_response: CT soft-marks evictions and reuses same-thought physical slots through masks and start indices.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 7 measures gather cost; Theorem 1 explains no reordering; Tables 2, 5, and 12 provide system comparisons.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion says CT manages memory without costly compactions.

claim_closure.claim: ThinKV delivers near-lossless accuracy with under 5% original KV cache and up to 5.8× throughput.
claim_closure.method_response: Combines thought decomposition, TBQ, TBE, and CT.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 8, Tables 1–3, Figure 9, and Table 4 provide task, baseline, and control evidence.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion repeats <5% cache and up to 5.8× throughput.

lexical_rhetoric.scope: Main-text raw scan, pp. 1–10, includes figure captions and table text; global aggregation owns canonical token counts.
lexical_rhetoric.strong_vs_weak_claim_pattern: Strong numeric claims cluster in Abstract, §1.2, §6.2, and Conclusion; scope and uncertainty qualifications occur mainly in §6, Appendix E, and Appendix F.

conclusion_analysis.boundary_or_future_work: not_present in the conclusion; limitation is Appendix F.

final_judgment.single_storyline: ThinKV treats thought-level sparsity as the bridge from LRM reasoning structure to hybrid KV compression, then makes non-contiguous eviction executable through CT slot reuse.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The main body keeps the resource bottleneck, four components, CT data structure, models/baselines/hardware, primary accuracy-throughput evidence, and core ablations.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: The appendix moves proofs, background, calibration algorithm, formats, pseudo-code, extended models/tasks, vLLM details, and long reasoning traces; this leaves the narrative understandable but makes CT correctness and reproduction details appendix-dependent.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 6 turns the algorithm-system coupling into one traceable object, while Table 2 pairs maximum-batch data with an iso-batch iso-compression control.
final_judgment.largest_gap: No seed values, error bars, intervals, or hypothesis tests accompany headline system and accuracy values; the explicit long-input limitation appears only in Appendix F.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a paper claiming both algorithmic and systems gains, pair the component causal diagram with a matched control that separates capacity effects from kernel-cost effects.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: Use that rule when a resource path and matched systems baseline exist; theory-only work needs comparable assumption and proof controls instead.

final_judgment_evidence.name: Storyline
final_judgment_evidence.description: Sparsity, TBQ, TBE, and CT are introduced in causal order.

final_judgment_evidence.name: Largest gap
final_judgment_evidence.description: The PDF reports 3-run averages and no further uncertainty presentation; F Limitations is on p. 34.
